scope: Proposition 4.1 (Marked subsequential limits) of the manuscript “Fixed-energy universality for weak Anderson disorder on random regular graphs” (preprints/Fixed-energy-universality-for-weak-Anderson-disorder-on-random-regular-graphs-October-5-2026/fixed-energy-universality-weak-anderson-disorder-random-regular-graphs.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 219 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b90d91abec2e8614), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every sequence of admissible sizes tending to infinity has a subsequence on which νn converges in law to a locally finite point measure ν. On a further subsequence one can retain jointly the positions and the empirical marked-neighborhood laws for the eigenvalue-ordered lists in an exhaustion by bounded intervals, together with all their finite truncations and restrictions. Repeated limiting positions retain separate marks. Almost every resulting empirical law L, with m colors, is an automorphism-invariant law on the d-regular tree, whose potential marginal is the deterministic iid uniform law on [−w, w]. If Uv ∈ Rm is its mark at v, then ELUoUT o = Im, (Vv − E)Uv + X u∼v Uu = 0 at every v. (36) The empirical laws and their restrictions to smaller lists can be chosen consistently.
